results.title: GPU Rental Prices Are Rising Again: What the October 2026 Nebius and AWS Changes Mean for Inference Cost
highlights:
After falling in 2025, H100 rental prices rose in 2026. Nebius raised list prices on 1 October and AWS raised Capacity Blocks on 7 October. Here is what the numbers show and how to plan for them.

...

In short

- GPU rental prices fell in 2025 and are rising in 2026. Nebius raised its H100 on-demand price from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour on 1 October 2026.
- AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks prices by about 15% in October. AWS on-demand prices did not change.
- One price index put the median on-demand H100 SXM at $4.20 per GPU-hour on 7 October 2026. Hyperscalers charged a median of $10.53 for the same GPU.
- The "price per GPU-hour" you see is a list price. Your real cost per token depends on utilization, and a half-idle GPU costs twice as much per token.
- Plan for price drift: use commitments for steady load, keep workloads portable, and track cost per token, not cost per hour.

...

## What changed in October 2026

Key point

Two large providers raised GPU prices within a week of each other, reversing the 2025 trend.

The Uvik GPU Price Index (captured 7 October 2026) lists the dated events. On 1 October, Nebius raised H100 on-demand from $3.85 to $4.50 (+17%). It raised H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (+20%). On 7 October, AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks prices by about 15%.

The Nebius pricing page I fetched today matches the new numbers. It lists H100 at $4.50, H200 at $5.40, B200 at $8.50 and B300 at $9.50 per GPU-hour. It also says prices may change at any time.

IntuitionLabs checked AWS on 10 October 2026. The Capacity Blocks rate for P5 (H100) is $5.970 per GPU. In July 2026 it was $5.191 in US regions and $4.720 in other regions. By my calculation from those figures, that is about +15% in the US and about +26.5% elsewhere. AWS says the rates are next scheduled to be updated in January 2027.

Note

Capacity Blocks are reservations, not on-demand. IntuitionLabs warns against using them for cross-provider comparison. AWS on-demand prices did not change in this round.

...

The Uvik index covers 19 providers and 87 public on-demand prices. It excludes spot, marketplace, reserved and contract-only prices. For the H100 SXM it found a median of $4.20, a low of $3.20 (Hyperstack and Thunder Compute) and a high of $12.29 (Microsoft Azure).

Split by type, the four hyperscalers had a median of $10.53. The 12 GPU clouds had a median of $3.95. That is a 2.7x gap. Across all GPUs in the index the hyperscaler multiple runs from 1.7x to 2.7x.

...

- After falling in 2025, GPU rental prices rose in 2026: on 1 October 2026 Nebius raised H100 on-demand from $3.85 to $4.50 (+17%) and H200 from $4.50 to $5.40; AWS raised EC2 Capacity Blocks by about 15% (a reservation product, not on-demand, which did not change; next update scheduled January 2027).
- The Uvik index (19 providers, 87 public on-demand prices) put the median H100 SXM at $4.20 per GPU-hour on 7 October, with a hyperscaler median of $10.53 versus $3.95 for 12 GPU clouds (2.7x). Three-year commitments cut H100 prices by 56% to 57% at the big three.
- Which provider you rent from matters more than the month you rent in.

...

results.title: Public Cloud: à la carte model starting October 1, 2026
results.author: Octave Klaba
highlights:
Public Cloud: à la carte model starting October 1, 2026 

# Public Cloud: the end of the all-in-one plan

Octave Klaba 25/08/2026 7 min read

Our Public Cloud instances have historically included local storage and a public IPv4 address in the same price. From October 1st, 2026, these two resources will become separate billable lines. The price of the virtual machine, or the compute, will not change.

With memory and storage costs rising, our goal is to minimize this impact on you. This means being able to choose what you actually need and in what quantity.

Even at the same configuration, your bill will increase. But you can act now: free up an unused IP address, choose a Flex instance that only takes up 50 GB of local disk, and add some remote Block Storage. Depending on your usage, the increase may be incremental at most.

...

### How much price rise are we talking about?

Between a 1.4% and 21.9% increase, depending on your size, with storage capacity unchanged.

The difference between these two numbers can be easily explained. Local storage is capped at 400 GB and the IP address costs a fixed amount, so the increase is almost the same, in euros, for all instances. For those of smaller scale, this amount may weigh more heavily. For the bigger scale, the increased amount becomes marginal. You can find price breakdown examples, instance by instance, in this article.

...

On Generation 3 instances, B3, C3, and R3 families, local storage is no longer included in the instance price. It is billed 0.0001458 € ex. VAT per GB and per hour, or about 0.11 € per GB and per month, or 109 € per TB and per month. On all previous ranges (B2, C2, R2 and earlier), it remains included.

...

VAT per hour, which is about €1.97 per

...

| --- | --- |
| 12 months | 15% off |
| 36 months | 30% off |

...

## Change schedule

| Date | Step |
| --- | --- |
| End of August 2026 | Update of the prices on the website |
| September 1, 2026 | Launch of the new Savings Plans Instances grid, informing of the clients concerned |

## What’s not changing

The hourly price of instances. The performance of our network. Powerful anti-DDoS included. Outbound traffic included. And our sovereign, European cloud.

results.title: OVHcloud Prices Rise on 1 October, at Your Renewal Date
results.author: Private DevOps LTD
highlights:
# OVHcloud Prices Rise on 1 October, at Your Renewal Date

August 30, 2026 6 min read

A fixed EUR 290 review prices your server in OVHcloud's new tables and sets out options.

Headlines say 87 percent. OVHcloud's own tables say up to 158 on servers and 652 on memory. What rises, what does not, and why 1 October matters.

...

OVHcloud is repricing its dedicated servers, and the reason is the one everybody in hosting has been watching since last autumn. In their own words, "DDR5 RAM now costs six times as much as it did a year ago", because the three companies that make memory have pointed their factories at the high-bandwidth kind that goes next to a GPU, without demand for the ordinary kind falling to match.

The company was explicit that it did not want a flat rise. Their teams went through the catalogue model by model, and the tables in their announcement show it: some configurations move by 5 percent and some by more than 150.

...

Coverage of this has settled on "up to 87 percent". That figure does appear in OVHcloud's announcement, next to one storage option, an eight-drive NVMe array going from 806 to 1,506 euros. It is not the ceiling for anything.

Here is what the configuration tables actually say, for new orders from 11 August 2026:

| Range | Increase |
| --- | --- |
| Advance, Gen 2024 | +16% to +131% |
| Advance, Gen 2026 | +25% to +158% |
| Game, Gen 2026 | +74% to +128% |
| Scale, Gen 2024 | +22% to +127% |
| Scale, Gen 2026 | +28% to +133% |
| High Grade, Gen 2024 | +5% to +42% |
| High Grade, Gen 2026 | +46% to +127% |

So the servers themselves go well past 87 percent in five of the seven ranges.

...

## Three Dates, and the One That Matters to You

OVHcloud published a schedule rather than a switch:

- 1 July 2026 - new rates for memory and storage options, on orders from that date
- 11 August 2026 - new configuration pricing, on new orders from that date
- 1 October 2026 - new rates on servers already running, taking effect on each subscription's renewal date

The first two have already happened and only affect what you buy next. 1 October is the one that reaches machines you are already running, and it does not arrive as a single invoice. It lands on each server when that server renews, so a fleet bought across a year will reprice across a year.

...

## What Is Not Affected

Worth saying plainly, because the headlines do not. The Kimsufi, So you Start and Rise ranges are not affected, and neither are generations before Gen 2024.

If your workloads sit on older hardware or on the budget lines, this announcement does not touch you. That covers a lot of the small production servers people actually run.

results.title: OVHcloud Raises Prices as AI Memory Demand Reprices Non-AI Infrastructure - InfoQ
results.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers
highlights:
# OVHcloud Raises Prices as AI Memory Demand Reprices Non-AI Infrastructure 

Aug 23, 2026 4 min read 

by

- Steef-Jan Wiggers 

OVHcloud will raise prices across most of its catalog this autumn, and the cause sits outside the products being repriced. Memory and storage costs have climbed steeply since mid-2025, and founder Octave Klaba traces that to the AI buildout pulling fabrication capacity away from the components every ordinary server is built from.

Klaba set out the mechanism in a post on X. Three global RAM suppliers have reconfigured their factories toward high-bandwidth memory, which serves GPUs and carries better margins, at the expense of standard DDR4 and DDR5. He posts in French, and the quotes here come from platform translations.

The numbers come from OVHcloud's own purchasing. Indexed to June 2025, memory reached 604 by June 2026, SSDs 323, and hard drives 148. Klaba's forecast goes further:

> This month, in June 2026, we're paying 6x the price for RAM that we paid in June 2025. We already know it will be x9 in September 2026, while forecasts for early 2027 are at x12!?

[Components inflation, indexed to June 2025 (Source: OVHcloud)]

He adds that NVMe drives are at 7x and hard drives at 3.5x, and reports hearing that CPUs, motherboards, and network cards will rise 15 to 20 percent.

The increases land unevenly. Renters of 2026-edition gaming servers face the steepest rise at 87 percent, while other recent servers go up 40 to 59 percent, all from September. Customers on 2024-era equipment see smaller increases at renewal, which Klaba puts at three to six times lower than a new order. Older ranges including Kimsufi, Rise, and earlier Advance and Scale generations are untouched, as they were in an April increase.

Some charges are also being restructured rather than raised. From October 1, storage and IP addresses become separate line items on Gen3 instances, at €0.000146 per GB per hour and €0.0027 per hour. OVHcloud is dropping its one-month, six-month, and 24-month saving plans, keeping the 12- and 36-month options that lock pricing for their duration.

...

Amazon buys in the same market and has moved almost nothing. It raised EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML, a reserved GPU product, by roughly 20 percent in July after about 15 percent in January, and left the rest of the catalog alone, including instances running Trainium, the accelerator it designs itself. The change appeared on the pricing page with no announcement, and the company said afterward only that Capacity Blocks prices are updated periodically based on supply and demand.

关键要点

- 由于价格上涨，数据中心投资回收期从 4-5 年缩短至约 2 年。

全球新云公司在发布第二季度财报期间纷纷强调 GPU 价格上涨。韩国投资证券分析指出，数据中心投资回收期已从此前的 4—5 年缩短至约 2 年。价格上涨源于企业 Token 用量快速增长，这表明类似变化最终可能影响韩国数据中心运营商。新云公司是指提供基于 GPU 的云计算服务、专门用于人工智能模型训练和推理的服务商。

results.title: OVHcloud warns: price hikes of up to 87% due to memory shortage - Techzine Global
results.author: Mels Dees
highlights:
OVHcloud is raising prices on some of its bare-metal and public cloud offerings. For recent bare-metal servers, the increases reach up to 87 percent. CEO Octave Klaba points primarily to the sharp rise in RAM and storage prices resulting from the AI boom.

...

For Gen 2024, the increase averages 28 percent; for Gen 2026, it averages 51 percent. Game Gen 2026 stands out as the biggest increase at 87 percent. New server configurations will be subject to the adjusted prices starting September 1. For existing equipment, the new rates will apply upon renewal starting October 1.

...

For Public Cloud, OVHcloud is leaving the compute price unchanged but is changing the pricing model. Low Latency Block Storage and IPv4 addresses, previously included with Gen3 instances, will be billed separately starting October 1.

As a result, according to Klaba, actual costs will rise by 1.4 to 21.9 percent, depending on the instance. Small instances in particular will be hit relatively harder, as the fixed costs for storage and an IP address carry more weight for them.

Managed Databases and Analytics will become 3.6 percent more expensive on average. MongoDB remains unchanged, as do Object Storage, High Availability Block Storage, and File Storage.

results.title: Server prices to rise by up to 87% at OVHcloud
results.author: Peter Sayer
highlights:
News Aug 11, 2026 4 mins

## Rising component costs are forcing the European cloud operator to increase bare metal and public cloud prices for new and existing customers. 

 

 Credit: OVHcloud 

OVH is increasing the prices of its servers, some by as much as 87%, for both new and existing customers, blaming AI’s insatiable demand driving the rising cost of the RAM and storage it uses in its data centers.

The European cloud operator specializes in low-cost bare metal and public cloud offerings.

...

The increases will hurt hard-core gamers hardest, with the cost of the company’s most recent gaming servers rising 87%. (Older gaming instances are unaffected.)

## High Grade, high price

But enterprises will also feel the pain from climbing component costs: OVH’s latest High Grade bare metal servers, with up to 2 x 96 cores of AMD Epyc 9005 series processors, 36 hard disks per server, and high-density cooling systems, will go up in price by 59%; older models built to the 2024 spec will go up 26%.

Lower-performance servers will also see increases of 40%-49% for the most recent models, and 26%-37% for older models.

The new prices take effect from Sept. 1 for new orders, and from Oct. 1 for renewals.

It’s not just baseline server prices that are increasing; optional additional memory and storage are going up in price too. OVH already increased the cost of these extras for new server orders as of July 1, with RAM prices rising 127% and disks 89%. From Oct. 1, renewals will be affected too, with the price of additional RAM in the latest servers rising by 40%, and that of larger disks by 15%. For servers built to 2024 specs, the increases will be 20% and 10% respectively.

Existing customers can lock in current prices for servers already in production for up to four years if they pay in advance by Oct. 1, Klaba wrote. Existing commitments will not be affected by the increases until they are due for renewal.

...

The price rises are more nuanced when it comes to public cloud systems. In future, OVH will break out storage and IP address rental costs separately, and will allow customers to mix and match storage capacity and compute.

“In appearance, hourly compute cost won’t change,” Klaba wrote. “On the other hand, low-latency Block Storage and IPv4 addresses, previously included in our Gen3 instances (B3, C3, R3) will appear as two separately billed line items on Oct. 1.”

The result is price increases of as little as 1.4% for the most powerful instances, or as much as 21.9% for smaller instances, he said.

OVH will continue to offer a 15% discount for a commitment of one year, or 30% for three years, he said, but will no longer offer discounts for shorter terms.

results.title: 1/4 Comme vous le savez, l'IA a un impact très important sur les prix de la RAM et du stockage que nous utilisons pour construire les serveurs de nos datacenters. | Octave Klaba
results.author: Octave Klaba
highlights:
En juillet et août, nous avons reçu les derniers éléments relatifs aux prix de la RAM et des disques pour T3/Q3 2026, ce qui nous permet désormais de statuer sur les impacts de prix pour les nouvelles commandes Public Cloud et Baremetal, ainsi que sur une partie récente du matériel déjà en production basé sur la dernière génération de RAM DDR5.

En effet, comme il y a 3-4 mois, en avril/mai, nous suivons la même idée: limiter les évolutions de prix unitaire du Public Cloud et du Baremetal, et être capables de livrer le matériel pour vos nouvelles commandes.

L'exercice reste acrobatique: il nous faut passer le bon volume de commandes, mois par mois, sur 12 mois, sans aucune garantie du prix d'achat et sans savoir quelle sera la vraie demande de nos clients.

Cela étant dit, même si nos prix augmentent, nous restons les moins chers du marché sur le Baremetal et sur le Public Cloud, là où nous pouvions être 3x moins cher, on passe à 2x moins cher (si nos concurrents n'augmentent pas leurs prix).

Voici les grandes lignes des modifications tarifaires du Q3 2026 chez OVHcloud.

Baremetal
-----------
• Comme en avril/mai, Kimsufi, So You Start et Rise ne bougent pas.

• Sur les nouvelles commandes, les options RAM et disques ont de nouveaux prix depuis le 1er juillet.

• Sur les nouvelles commandes, les configurations de serveur passent aux nouveaux tarifs le 1er septembre.

• Le matériel déjà en production est concerné par l'évolution de prix au renouvellement, à partir du 1er octobre, sur Advance, Game, Scale et High Grade, sur la Gen 2024 et la Gen 2026.

• Voici la hausse moyenne par référence:
· Kimsufi, So You Start, Rise: 0 %
· Game: Gen 2024: 0 %, Gen 2026: +87 %
· Advance: Gen 2024: +26 %, Gen 2026: +49 %
· Scale: Gen 2024: +37 %, Gen 2026: +40 %
· High Grade: Gen 2024: +26 %, Gen 2026: +59 %
Soit +28 % en moyenne sur la Gen 2024, et +51 % sur la Gen 2026.

• Sur les options déjà installées sur le parc existant, nous appliquons un barème réduit: RAM +20 % sur la Gen 2024 et +40 % sur la Gen 2026 au lieu de +127 %, disques +10 % et +15 % au lieu de +89 %. Un client déjà équipé aura donc une hausse 3 à 6 fois plus faible que pour une nouvelle commande.

• Rien ne change pendant un engagement en cours.

• Pour figer votre prix actuel dans la durée, vous pouvez souscrire 12, 24 ou 48 mois avec paiement upfront. À faire avant le 1er octobre pour un serveur déjà en production.
